title: Man. Post. Cap. X: PLAC — what of real corruption until the law? That helps Pighius/Pelagius
pass_a_gloss: Next: what of the corruption that truly is sin and really was in all men until the law? Why should Paul’s usual ‘sin’ not mean that here? Could the learned man invent anything that helps Pighius—even Pelagius—more?
pass_b_english: Next, what will become of the corruption which truly is sin, and really was in all men until the law?
What reason is there why it ought not to be understood under the name of sin in this place, after the Apostle’s manner?
Could the learned man invent anything that would more help the cause of Pighius—nay, of Pelagius?
source_text: Deinde quid fiet de corruptione quae vere peccatum est, & revera fuit in omnibus hominibus usque ad legem? Quid est cur peccati nomine hoc loco, pro Apostoli more, non debeat intelligi? Potuitne Vir doctus quicquam comminisci, quod magis causam Pighii, imo Pelagii, iuvaret?

choices.choice: Real corruption until the law fits Paul’s ‘sin’
